🇪🇺🇺🇸 Europe’s independent space-based reconnaissance capabilities ‘almost zero’ without US
 
European countries are reportedly in no condition to do deep-strike targeting without US assistance.
🔊 “If we look at the space capabilities of the Europeans in terms of [Intelligence, Surveillance, and Reconnaissance, they are] not a whole lot – actually, almost zero without the US,” an anonymous European NATO commander told The Times on Thursday.
US space assets provide some ~85% of NATO’s centralized military intelligence reports, leaving European militaries essentially blind if Washington were to restrict access, the newspaper reported.
Individual countries like France, Germany and Italy operate their own satellites, but don’t have the global scale, refresh rate or real-time presence that the US enjoys to sustain targeting. Furthermore, a March 2026 IISS report found that Europe’s militaries are hopelessly dependent on US infrastructure for other things, like missile early warning, heavy-lift launches and satellite tracking.
Europe hopes to close the gap using a number of measures, including:
🔴 shaking up the European Space Agency’s peaceful mandate to include defense objectives, including a ~$1.5B commitment for “non-aggressive” security and dual-use capabilities, like high-res Earth observation, satellite surveillance, secure communications
🔴 national investments, with Germany greenlighting ~$1.9B for a new 40-unit satellite synthetic aperture radar constellation called Spock-1, and talking to Norway about new potential ISR capabilities
🔴 purchases of SAR capabilities from [Iceye](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/76506), a private Finnish satellite operator
Europe’s search for independent satellite intelligence capabilities come in the wake of the US’s temporary halting of[ intel transfers](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/73284) to Kiev amid the Ukraine war to try to force it to the negotiating table.

🇮🇷🚀 IRGC says sanctions can’t stop missile production – Western intel confirms capacity intact, growing
 
IRGC chief Ahmad Vahidi has issued a message of defiance to Iran’s enemies, warning that “the path of Martyr Hassan Tehrani Moqaddam [the late father of Iran’s missile program, ed.] is one that cannot be halted by threats or sanctions.”
🔊 “Today,” the IRGC Aerospace Force is “building power in the heart of mountains and deep underground to make the country stronger,” Vahidi said, referencing [growing firepower at Iran’s underground ‘missile cities’](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/77627) – which have [proven largely impregnable to US-Israeli strikes](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/75210).
Secretary of War Pete Hegseth maintains US strikes have crippled Iran’s ability to produce missiles and that the country’s defense industrial base is essentially “gone.”
But an unnamed Western official told Bloomberg this week that Western intelligence believes Iran possesses at least 1.7k ballistic missiles in its inventory, and is producing more at a rate of ~50 per month, about half of its prewar rate, after firing off ~2.2k since February. 
Iran has not disclosed the number of missiles it has, or its capacity to produce new ones. However, Iranian political commentator Mohammad Marandi said recently that Iran had converted its industries to a wartime economy, and been replenishing its arsenal so quickly it’s running out of places to store new weapons – directly countering US claims.

events.text:
🇺🇸💵 Pentagon Inc: Trump’s Department of War taking control of private industry
The Department of War’s growing number of investments, purchases and hostile takeovers of private companies threatens to “transform” the agency from a “power unto itself within the government to something that transcends it – an independent economic behemoth” rivalling the structure of some Middle Eastern militaries, a new report highlighted by The Intercept suggests.
Exploring this modern-day version of Oliver North’s Iran-Contra era “Enterprise,” which endowed the stand-alone Reagan-era covert action cut out with immense, oversight-free economic power, Rebecca Gordon of TomDispatch argues that the modern Pentagon equivalent may be [much worse](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/49581).
 
In the past 22 months alone, the DoW has:
🔴 been granted a 35% ownership stake in[ North American Blue Energy Partners (NABEP)](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/76664), a new company given a 100-year concession to extract ~65B barrels of crude from Venezuela, plus exclusive rights to buy 20% of NABEP’s output ‘at cost’, following January’s soft coup
🔴 invested heavily into rare earth minerals mining, processing and recycling, including Vulcan Elements ($620M loan, $50M equity stake), [MP Materials](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/72006) ($400M for 15% stake), Korea Zinc ($1.9B, 40% ownership), ReElement ($80M for stock rights) and Trilogy Metals (equity stake for $35.6M)
🔴 other industrial investments, including in steelmaker Hertha Metals ($65M + unknown number of shares), tungsten producer Elmet Group ($450M equity) and iron producer Hertha Metals ($65M equity)
🔴 direct investments into defense contractors themselves, including a $1B equity deal with missile maker L3Harris, a 40% ownership stake in[ Anduril Industries’ new sub shipyard](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/75761), and a $450M loan to drone maker Neros Technologies in exchange for non-voting equity stake.
 
[The DoD’s new policy](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/74322) has been made possible by the Office of Strategic Capital, the Economic Defense Unit and the Office of Industrial Base Policy. These offices have major reported links to Trump donors and allies, including billionaire Stephen Feinberg (DoD undersecretary), and[ the Trump family itself](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/70348) (which invested in Vulcan Elements and MP Materials before their Pentagon buy-ins, for example).
